newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., seeks outside audit of seaport. [CORRECTED 22:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., seeks outside audit of seaport. [CORRECTED 22:25 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects throughout that memo was written by Dade County Mayor to County Manager Armando Vidal, instead of written by Vidal.)
Florida's Dade County mayor requested an outside audit of the Port of Miami and a review of other county departments, saying an internal seaport audit had raised serious financial concerns.
An internal audit, released last week, said the seaport had a cash flow deficit of $22 million.

"Certainly the findings of the auidit are troubling and of serious concerns to Dade County taxpayers," County Mayor Alex Penelas said in a memo to County Manager Armando Vidal and county commissioners late Monday.
"These reports have raised public concern as to the overall financial health of the Port of Miami and the viablity of the proposed Port expansion," Penelas said.
The port had planned to borrow $47 million as part of an expansion project that would include new cruise ship berths and a basketball arena to be built by the Miami Heat.
Penelas also asked that county comissioners "seek an assurance of sound financial condition through documented opinion" from the county's aviation, water and sewer and solid waste departments.
The aviation department runs Miami International Airport.
In a separate memo, Penelaas recommended that Port of Miami Director Carmen Lunetta, who abruptly announced his retirement during the weekend, be allowed to help choose his replacement.
Penelas praised Lunetta, noting he "has worked very hard over the past 38 years to make our port a world leader in both the cruise and cargo industries."
He recommended that an international search be launched to find a new seaport director, and asked the county commission to submit a search plan by Friday.
Penelas urged the commission to appoint an interim transition team whose tasks will include a review of all port services, contracts and operations.

"In consideration of his being port director for the past 18 years and the tremendous institutional knowledge and hisotry associated therewith, I recommend that Carmen Lunetta also be a member" of the transition team, Penelas wrote in the memo.

Lunetta, 67, announced his resignation during the weekend, after The Miami Herald reported that port money was spent on Super Bowl tickets, luxury car rentals and campaign contributions, including contributions to current county commissioners.
